ai.description: The Kumbara Night Frog is a small, brown amphibian (25–35 mm). It features a distinct, pointed snout and prominent, fleshy femoral glands in males. It inhabits high-altitude stream environments.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus kumbara* is best distinguished by the prominent, fleshy, spine-like tubercle located at the tip of its snout, a unique feature absent in other night frogs.
ai.habitat: The Kumbara night frog inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found near small, slow-flowing streams within dense, shaded canopy cover.
ai.behavior: The Kumbara Night Frog is strictly nocturnal and exhibits unique parental care, where males guard egg clutches laid on overhanging vegetation near forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus kumbara* exhibits direct development and lays terrestrial clutches of 20–30 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Kumbara night frog is endemic to the central Western Ghats in Karnataka, India, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Kumbara Night Frog produces a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "ticking" notes, typically heard while the frogs are perched on rocks near fast-flowing forest streams.
